ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ACB$, $\angle ACB=90^\circ$, point M is the midpoint of side $AB$, point E is on segment $AM$, $EF\perp AC$ at point F, connect $CM$, $CE$. It is known that $\angle A=50^\circ$, $\angle ACE=30^\circ$, and $CE=CM$. If $AB=4$, find the length of segment $FC$.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $AB=4$,\\
it follows that $CE=CM=\frac{1}{2}AB=2$,\\
since $EF\perp AC$ and $\angle ACE=30^\circ$,\\
it follows that $EF=\frac{1}{2}CE=1$,\\
therefore $FC=\sqrt{CE^{2}-EF^{2}}=\sqrt{2^{2}-1^{2}}=\boxed{\sqrt{3}}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is a right triangle ACB, point C is at the lower left, AC is vertical upward, CB is horizontal to the right, and AB is the hypotenuse; M is marked on the hypotenuse AB, and E is also on the part AM of the hypotenuse near A; from E draw a horizontal line to the left to AC, with intersection point F, indicating EF is perpendicular to AC; line segments CE and CM both connect from C to points on the hypotenuse. Reasoning: In right triangle ACB, M is the midpoint of the hypotenuse AB, so the midpoint of the hypotenuse is equidistant from the three vertices, CM=AB/2. It is known that AB=4, therefore CM=2. It is also known that CE=CM, so CE=2. Because EF⊥AC and F is on AC, triangle CFE is a right triangle, and CE is the hypotenuse. Also because CF and CA are on the same straight line, ∠ECF=∠ACE=30°. Therefore FC=CE·cos30°=2·(√3/2)=√3.
